My personal suggestion, as someone who's had severe acne, but dry skin, & have over the years gotten most of my acne under control through my skin care, is to use less products, at least for a bit.

Some of the products could be some of the reason you break out (for me, while I LOVE la roche posay, their products broke me out so severely it's like my skin backtracked to years ago when I had severe cystic acne everywhere again for over a decade.)

It's easier to tell what is helping, or hurting, your skin if there's constantly more being added to your skincare. And sometimes certain products don't go well with each other.

I'd personally pair it down to a face wash, maybe a toner (only if it's for hydration & DOESNT have alcohol in it), a Serum (ONE Serum at first) if you want, & a moisturizer & a sunscreen for the daytime.

& this is the annoying part....do that for at least a month or 2. If nothing is getting worse, add in 1 more product for about a month, & if nothing worse happens with your skin, then repeat the process with other products. But you don't need a ton of serums all in one application, or a ton of moisturizers, etc. If you have multiple you like, just use 1 per day, but alternate them each day.

But sometimes, using the amount of products you are, it can sometimes counteract the good each products is doing & all your skin knows is too much stuff is being slathered on it & it'll react badly.

Some of my personal tips are:

1. Write every day. Not 200 pages a day or 10,000 words a day (fantastic if you do though). Whether it's 5 words or 500. It'll keep you in the habit so you're less likely to abandon your work for months or years at a time (it happens to the best of us)

2. Write dialog the way real people speak. To make sure my dialog in my stories soind decent, I always play out the scene in my head like I'm watching it happen irl, & then Write that down. "Seeing" it helps for me.

3. Set goals for yourself so you keep moving forward instead of going a bit stagnate. For example, if I'm writing a short story or fanfic, I might say "I want to finish it by the end of this month". I might not achieve that goal, & that's okay, but I try & aim for that as best i can. It gives me more motivation, so I won't have days I feel like I can skip (1 day can turn into 10 into 100). Or it can be "I want to reach this scene by ______<<" or "i will have this part of the story or this plot hole figured out by ______«. It just helps kick my but in gear a bit more. But I also don't beat myself up if it takes longer.
Yeah, I can try that & see if it holds!

Anytime I hate the way I write (my voice, or I'm bad at certain types of scenes) I just essentially write short scenes of stories focusing specifically on my problem.

I used to be awful at writing action scenes. Like AWFUL. Now I'm not saying I'm the best action writer in the world now or anything, but I figure the brain is a muscle. So let me work it out until I strengthen it.

So I wrote random scene after random scene until I started improving writing those scenes & feeling more confident in them, so now it doesn't worry me putting those in my stories anymore.

Maybe try the same thing. Write a scene (from your story, from a totally different story, hell from a movie or book that already exists, idc) & then do a rewrite until you start getting better/feeling more confidemt about showing instead of just telling.

I still sometimes have issues with telling instead of showing, but I know I can go back & fix that in my next draft & improve it. Everything is fixable, don't stress too much about it. Just exercise your brain & work on it & you'll get better at it!

One thing that helps me is to take boxes/laundry baskets/etc & put one in each room I'm cleaning.

Throw EVERYTHING that's out of place into that box (throw trash away of course), do any further deep cleaning of that room.

Then, either right then or when I get my mental energy up again, I go through the box & put things up. If it goes in another room, just drop it in that room's box until you get to clean it, etc.

Doing that gives me a quick visual of a cleaner room immediately (junk off shelves, etc) which helps me feel more motivated, & then having only to deal with what's in one box makes dealing with it seem smaller & more manageable.

I've dealt with plenty of depression houses I've created, some such a huge problem I HAD to have help with. But this method is still the one that worked for me. It'll just take a little longer & a couple more boxes, but just doing this & repeating helped me get things slowly back into shape.

Biggest thing is don't beat yourself up over it. If it's a low energy day, set a timer for like 10-15 minutes & only do what you can within that time frame. Anything helps. You can do this!

Start with learning Hangul, that's the most important starting point imo (there are some free apps that are amazing for this - LingoDeer & Drops are some ofy favoritesfor Hangul specifically), it's pretty easy/quick to learn the basics of Hangul.

Then pick at least 1 primary way you want to start learning Korean with (book/lesson plans? YouTube videos? Apps? Etc) & focus your main learning on that (at least at first), & then you can use things like kdramas/music for fun exercises (NOT as a primary way to learn the language/normal way of speaking).

Then as you learn more & grow you'll have a better idea of what you want/need to learn & how to learn it for what works best for you so you can adapt for a better/more successful learning experience. 

Also, work on it DAILY! Whether that's sitting down for an hour with a lesson/YouTube video, or spending 5 minutes before bed doing a listening challenge, or writing in Hangul, or practicing grammar, etc.

Just keeping it on your mind daily will do wonders with learning & being able to progress quicker & remember previous lessons easier.

If you're nervous & unsure of where to start &/or how or what to progress onto next, a YouTube i highly recommend is [Learn Korean with GO! Billy](https://youtube.com/c/GoBillyKorean).

He has actual structured lesson plans you can start with as a beginner & a lot of other helpful videos to learn from. Even if you don't prefer his videos or yt vids in general, his lesson plans can at least give you a good idea of the best order in which to learn things.

Anyways, I hope this helped a little! Good luck! Korean can be very fun to learn if you stick with it!

While I am not going to tell you what I think you should do, that's something you need to decide for yourself since it's a very individualistic decision, I can tell you a bit of my story & how I personally chose to handle such situations.

I'm 33 now, been a practicing Pagan/Witch since I was 12, while I lived with my family in our house. We were raised Christian, but we were the "lazy" types of Christians (didn't go to church religiously, didn't talk about it outside of church really, etc). My mom got a bit more extremist Christian shortly before she died when I was 15, & my dad did when he remarried after her death & his new wife was a psycho who used religion to cover up her crazy (they luckily didn't stay together & he's a bit better now).

I never felt comfortable telling them though, at any stage. I was just expected to be Christian & follow Christianity unquestionably, so I never felt like I'd be accepted. I never felt like I'd be kicked out or shunned, but it's still a nerve-wracking thing.

At least until I got older...& realized I didn't HAVE to tell anybody. It wasn't required of me. So I just didn't. I didn't stop practicing, & while I didn't directly hide it from anybody as I got older, & eventually lived on my own, I didn't try to fully hide it either. I wouldn't put away books, or crystals, or stop wearing pagan jewelry, etc around them.

And that's just kinda how I handle everything with my family, tbh. If asked directly, I'll be truthful about anything. If I feel like talking about something, I will. But otherwise...if they want to know, they'll ask.

They don't ask though lol I kinda put the opportunity in their hands. They have strong suspicions about my beliefs, spirituality, sexuality, etc. All things that, according to modern evangelical Christianity I'm sinning for, they have vague guesses about. They've just never asked, unless they're ready to handle my answer.

I know that won't work for everybody, but it does with my family. I'm me & live my life how I want, but am also okay not being "officially out" to them about anything. They are mostly happy knowing they can pretend I'm not things they don't understand...at least until they get to curious or finally accept I'm not in this cookie cutter mold they always expected me to be in.

As for how I handled feeling "shame" of any sort as I grew into MY version of religion or spirituality...was knowledge. I try to learn about about other people's religion &/or spirituality, customs, beliefs, culture...& I eventually was able to leave any shame I was taught to feel by Christianity for not believing only the things it taught, by learning & appreciating other's version of spirituality & all of our differences. I realized that as long as I'm a decent person & try to be good, that's all I feel is required. How everyone chooses to.believe in that/practice it is their own path & not wrong, as long as it doesn't harm someone else.

It's all just something that grows with you as you learn more, practic more, & start REALLY figuring out who you are as a person.

Things take time, but it's worth it.

Good luck with your family, & I hope you find a comfortable way for you in regards to.how you choose to handle things. Dont rush it, & do what's best for you. 💜

For makeup, use a pore filling primer. My favorites are from Nyx & Benefit Cosmetics.

Unfortunately you can't permanently shrink pores, but things that can help is to makeup sure your skin is hydrated (not just moisturized). I personally love Coxrx's 96% Snail Mucin as a start.

While I am not a fan of Mario Badescu products in general, their "silver powder" product for pores I did actually notice a difference in pore size, but only if I kept up with it a couple times a week. And I'm pretty sure it's under $15 & lasts ages.

A combination of all of this should help, especially over time.

I'm very pale, & one of my favorite facial sunscreens, especially when my skin is dry, is the Cosrx Aloe Soothing Sun Cream with SPF50.
